name: Carmine (M&P)
lede: Carmine (M&P) is a variant swatch of [[carmine]], the name as Maerz and Paul charted it in their 1930 color dictionary, and brighter than the pigment it names.

sections.title: One plate's carmine
sections.body: Carmine itself is the historic crimson made from the cochineal insect, ground and used as a dye and pigment for centuries. This particular swatch is not that history; it is a single plate's reading of carmine, catalogued by Maerz and Paul in 1930 and carried into Wikipedia's color lists under their name [1]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[crimson|Crimson]], only 2.8 units away and read as almost the same color [2]; [[cherry|Cherry]] sits close behind, likewise near enough to call the same hue [2]. [[lipstick|Lipstick]] sits a little further out, read as darker by comparison [2].

sections.title: Brighter than the dye
sections.body: At hex #D70040, this swatch reads as a near-neon pink-red on screen, more saturated than the duller, brownish-red crimson that ground cochineal actually produces once mixed into paint or cloth [1]. The mismatch is ordinary for a historic dye name: a single printed plate, scanned decades later, sets the screen value, not a sample of the dye itself [1]. Treat this swatch as one witness among several: Wikipedia's own Carmine page lists other hex values closer to the duller, brick-red carmine most painters and dyers would recognize [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color appears in a single painting in our 23,781-painting archive, as photographed, rarer than 86 percent of our named colors [3].
